clue.text: Spotted in Tours, the French composer's happy

blocks.note: T' is the dialect, chiefly northern English, shortening of 'the'
Maurice Ravel, the French composer, with the possessive kept
oiled is slang for tipsy, merrily drunk

explanation.surface: A French composer is cheerful while touring the Loire city of Tours.
explanation.walkthrough: Tours looks like the French city, but the definition reads it as journeys. 'The' gives only T', its clipped dialect form.
explanation.definitionFit: Travel-soiled describes clothes or luggage stained and grubby from journeying, so marked or spotted on tours.

clue.text: Topless celebs overlooking American city of St Paul

indicators.note: without a top means the first letter of the word below it is cut off
in a down entry, to overlook is to sit above, so the first piece is written over the second

blocks.note: celebrities are stars
US for American

explanation.surface: Bare-chested celebrities gazing down on an American city named after a saint.
explanation.walkthrough: St Paul looks like the city in Minnesota, but the definition means the apostle, whose birthplace was in Cilicia, now southern Turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostle Paul was born in Tarsus, an ancient city of Cilicia, as Acts records.

clue.text: Make good turn in a single attempt

blocks.note: to atone is to make amends, make good a wrong
a turn in a game is a go

explanation.surface: Someone redeems themselves by succeeding on their first try.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'at one go' means all together in one effort, without a second try.

clue.text: Card game of very little interest

blocks.note: V is the abbreviation for very
a little, shortened interest: INT is its abbreviation

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a card game as being of hardly any interest.
explanation.definitionFit: Vint is a Russian card game resembling whist and bridge, listed in Chambers.

clue.text: After ending of performance, American composer half ignored bores

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept
ignoring half a name means only its first half is used, the back half dropped
after places what follows behind the first piece in the reading order

blocks.note: the last letter of performance
George Gershwin, the American composer

explanation.surface: After a show ends, half of an American composer's work is ignored by tedious people.
explanation.walkthrough: Bores looks like tedious people, but here it means tidal waves in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: An eger, or eagre, is a tidal bore: a wave surging up an estuary such as the Severn.

clue.text: One perhaps off to take in blue mineral

indicators.note: off means wrong or out of order, so these letters are rearranged
taking something in means holding it inside, so the rearranged word swallows the next piece

blocks.note: Roman numeral one
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who is perhaps leaving takes in a blue mineral.
explanation.walkthrough: The shuffled letters make a blue gem, which then takes IN before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapphirine is a sapphire-blue or greenish silicate mineral of magnesium and aluminium.

clue.text: Give line designed to persuade by flattery

indicators.note: something designed is arranged or made up, so these letters are set out anew

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A salesman spins a line meant to win someone over with flattery.
explanation.definitionFit: To inveigle is to coax or entice someone by cajolery and smooth talk.

clue.text: Woodworkers good in different sites

indicators.note: different means changed, so these letters take a new order
in puts one piece inside the rearranged letters

blocks.note: bon is French for good
taken as written

explanation.surface: Carpenters are doing good work at several building sites.
explanation.definitionFit: An ebonist is a worker in ebony, a craftsman of fine wood, so a woodworker.

clue.text: Silver coins given by father with stacks reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard spoken, so the word is matched by its sound

blocks.note: Da is an informal name for father
ricks are stacks of hay or straw

explanation.surface: Dad hands out silver coins along with whole piles of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Darics were ancient Persian coins; the gold daric had a silver counterpart, the siglos, also called a silver daric.

clue.text: Islander who's opposed to tagging noisy bird

indicators.note: tagging on means attaching one thing to the end of another

blocks.note: anti means against
a guan is a loud-calling turkey-like bird of tropical America

explanation.surface: An islander objects to tagging a loud bird.
explanation.definitionFit: An Antiguan is a native of Antigua, the Caribbean island.

clue.text: Forte hotel for a northerner

blocks.note: F is the musical abbreviation for forte, loud
an inn is a small hotel

explanation.surface: A Forte hotel, one of the British chain, is chosen for a visitor from the north.
explanation.walkthrough: Forte looks like the hotel group's name but gives only the music abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A Finn comes from Finland, a Nordic country in the far north of Europe.

clue.text: Hard right backed by a certain French department

indicators.note: backed means turned back to front, so the pair is read the other way round
by means beside, so the next piece follows on

blocks.note: H for hard, as on pencils
R for right
a certain person is 'one'

explanation.surface: A hard-right politician gains support from a particular region of France.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhône is a department of eastern France, named after the river, with Lyon as its seat.

clue.text: Cook arranges case of chive and seaweed

definitions.note: a mass noun standing for a plural answer

indicators.note: to cook is to doctor or falsify, so these letters are mixed up
the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

blocks.note: taken as written
the outer letters of chive

explanation.surface: A chef sets out a dish of chives and seaweed.
explanation.definitionFit: Carrageen, Irish moss, is an edible purplish red seaweed used for jellies and puddings.

clue.text: One to position flags in Washington with a VIP out in front of soldiers

definitions.text: One to position flags in Washington

indicators.note: out means wrong or out of place, so these letters are rearranged
in front of puts one piece before the next

blocks.note: taken as written
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Someone arranges flags in Washington, a VIP marching ahead of the troops.
explanation.walkthrough: Flags look like banners, but here they are flagstones; 'in Washington' marks the American spelling, without the U of British paviour.
explanation.definitionFit: A pavior lays paving stones, and flags are flat paving slabs, so the word means a paving layer.

clue.text: Fool takes wrong turn for hot spot

indicators.note: wrong means incorrect, so the next word's letters are put in a new order
taking something means holding it inside

blocks.note: a sap is a fool
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fool takes the wrong road and ends up somewhere sweltering.
explanation.definitionFit: A suntrap is a sheltered sunny place that catches the heat, a warm location.

clue.text: Sesame Street dropped by top names in short

indicators.note: dropped by means left out of, so these letters are removed from the following word
in short means the word is abbreviated to a single letter

blocks.note: ST is the abbreviation for street
best means top, supreme
nn. is the plural abbreviation of names
taken as written

explanation.surface: Top names drop out of the children's show Sesame Street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sesame Street' reads as the television show, but only Sesame is the definition. Street comes out of BEST, and IN is cut to I.
explanation.definitionFit: Benni, or bene, is another name for the sesame plant and its seeds.

clue.text: Standard rent said to be for bedding arrangement

indicators.note: said means as heard spoken, so what is written follows the sound

blocks.note: par is the standard, the norm
a rent is a tear or rip, which sounds like the French word for earth

explanation.surface: A standard rent is quoted for some beds being arranged.
explanation.walkthrough: Rent looks like money for housing, but it is a rip; bedding means flower beds.
explanation.definitionFit: A parterre is a formal garden of ornamental flower beds laid out in a pattern.

clue.text: Beat repetition brings trouble for playwright's editor

blocks.note: mall is an old verb meaning to maul or beat
an echo is a repetition of sound

explanation.surface: Repeated beats cause problems for an editor of a playwright's work.
explanation.walkthrough: The playwright is Shakespeare: Hamlet's 'miching mallecho' is a hard word for an editor to gloss.
explanation.definitionFit: Mallecho is Shakespeare's word for mischief or wrongdoing, as given in some editions of Hamlet.

clue.text: Police officer with cold brought around home remedy

indicators.note: brought around means turned about, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: DI is a Detective Inspector
in means at home
C for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A police officer with a chill is brought back home for a cure.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinic is a medicine for dizziness, a rare word meaning a remedy for vertigo.

clue.text: French novelist in hospital saving a grand

indicators.note: saving means keeping safe, holding something within

blocks.note: a san is a sanatorium
A plus G, a grand being a thousand

explanation.surface: A French writer in hospital manages to save a thousand pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Françoise Sagan was the French novelist who wrote Bonjour Tristesse.

clue.text: Fish good for number in band

indicators.note: for here means in place of, swapping one letter for another

blocks.note: G for good
N for number
a ring is a band

explanation.surface: A singer is replaced by a fish in a band's number.
explanation.walkthrough: Number looks like a song, but it just gives N, which is swapped out for G.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigg is a dialect name for the dogfish, a small shark.

clue.text: Protein a German has ingested finally

indicators.note: ingested means swallowed, so one word goes inside another

blocks.note: ein is German for a
last means finally

explanation.surface: A German has at last eaten some protein.
explanation.definitionFit: Elastin is the elastic fibrous protein found in connective tissue such as skin and arteries.

clue.text: Goddess seen in this moving augmented reality

indicators.note: moving means shifting position, so these letters change order

blocks.note: taken as written
AR is the abbreviation for augmented reality

explanation.surface: A goddess appears in a moving piece of augmented-reality technology.
explanation.definitionFit: Ishtar was the Babylonian and Assyrian goddess of love, fertility and war.

clue.text: Royal plainly losing 100

indicators.note: losing means going without, so these letters are taken away

blocks.note: clear as an adverb, as in speak clear, means plainly
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: A royal clearly loses a hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: King Lear is Shakespeare's tragic monarch, so royalty in literature.

clue.text: Being poor it's hard passing over a couple of pounds

indicators.note: passing over means going across and around something, here around a pair of letters

blocks.note: taken as written, the 's being 'has'
two Ls, L being the pound sign
H for hard

explanation.surface: Being poor is hard, with a couple of pounds passing by.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruskin coined this word as the opposite of wealth.
explanation.definitionFit: Illth is poverty or misery, the condition of lacking wealth, as Ruskin defined it.

clue.text: Harry lashes out

indicators.note: out means disordered, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man called Harry hits out at someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry looks like a name, but it is the verb to harass.
explanation.definitionFit: To harry is to pester or harass persistently, which is what hassling does.

clue.text: Bird in small hut

blocks.note: S for small
a tilt is an awning or tent cover, a kind of hut

explanation.surface: A bird is sheltering in a tiny shed.
explanation.definitionFit: The stilt is a long-legged wading bird of the avocet family.

clue.text: Russian typically with stake in Iran

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the letters that follow

blocks.note: IR is Iran's international vehicle code
go means bet or stake, as in 'I'll go twenty on that'

explanation.surface: A typical Russian has a financial stake in Iran.
explanation.definitionFit: Igor is a typical Russian man's first name, as with the composer Stravinsky.

clue.text: Rush up north for Jewish bond

blocks.note: first meaning: a northern dialect word for sedge or a rush-like grass
second meaning: a deed or bond in Hebrew, historically from Jews in England

explanation.surface: Someone hurries northwards to secure a Jewish bond.
explanation.walkthrough: Rush looks like a verb of hurrying, but it is the plant; 'up north' marks the northern dialect.
explanation.definitionFit: Starr is both a northern word for sedge grass and an old Hebrew legal deed or acquittance in medieval England.

clue.text: Philosopher on what's put over

indicators.note: put over means flipped, so the combined pair is read backwards

blocks.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side
eh is a request to repeat, like 'what?'

explanation.surface: A philosopher reflects on what has been delivered.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on side is also called the leg side, the half of the field behind the batsman's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Georg Hegel was the German idealist philosopher of the dialectic.

clue.text: Slight swelling in part of hospital with no change

blocks.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department
'as is' means unaltered

explanation.surface: A minor swelling appears on a hospital ward, unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: Entasis is the slight outward curve given to a column's shaft to correct optical illusion.

clue.text: Tapir seen up in Indian capital? Not the first

indicators.note: not the first means the opening letter is dropped
up in a down entry means read from bottom to top

blocks.note: Patna is the capital of the Indian state of Bihar

explanation.surface: A tapir is spotted in the capital of India.
explanation.walkthrough: Indian capital suggests Delhi, but the question mark allows a state capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Anta is a name for the tapir, the South American hoofed mammal.

clue.text: Toshiba's premier line about right for a tablet

indicators.note: premier means first, so only the opening letter is kept
about here means alongside, setting the darts line next to the other piece

blocks.note: the first letter of Toshiba
R for right
the oche is the line darts players throw from

explanation.surface: A Toshiba executive's product line is just about right for a tablet computer.
explanation.walkthrough: Tablet suggests a computer, but it is a medicinal lozenge.
explanation.definitionFit: A troche is a medicated lozenge, a small tablet dissolved in the mouth.

clue.text: French city disallowing capital payments in advance

indicators.note: disallowing its capital means the head letter is not allowed in

blocks.note: Nantes, the city on the Loire

explanation.surface: A French city refuses its capital investment up front.
explanation.definitionFit: Antes are stakes put up before play, or more widely advance payments.

clue.text: Arising from energy shortage, Institute latrine out of order

indicators.note: out of order means disarranged, so these letters are shuffled

blocks.note: I for Institute
taken as written

explanation.surface: Power cuts leave an institute's toilet broken.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is sluggishness or lack of energy, so something inertial stems from that lack.

clue.text: Protest about Belgian town's sleepy state

blocks.note: re means about, concerning
Mons is a town in Belgium; the 's is 'has'
a trance is a dreamy, half-asleep state

explanation.surface: A protest is lodged about a Belgian town's drowsiness.
